title: @PreAuthorize
question: What does @PreAuthorize do in Spring Security? Give an example with hasRole and hasAuthority.
realWorldScenario: Restricting admin-only controller or service methods to users with the ADMIN role.

title: @EnableMethodSecurity
question: Why do you need @EnableMethodSecurity? What was the older annotation in Spring Security 5?
searchIntent: how to enable method level security spring

title: hasRole vs hasAuthority
question: What is the difference between hasRole('ADMIN') and hasAuthority('ROLE_ADMIN') in Spring Security?
realWorldScenario: hasRole prepends ROLE_ automatically — hasAuthority does not. Mixing them causes authorisation failures.

title: @Secured Annotation
question: What is @Secured in Spring Security? How does it compare to @PreAuthorize?
realWorldScenario: @Secured is simpler but less flexible than @PreAuthorize — cannot use SpEL expressions.

title: @PostAuthorize
question: What is @PostAuthorize in Spring Security? When do you need post-execution authorisation instead of pre-execution?
realWorldScenario: A user can only see their own orders — @PostAuthorize checks returnObject.userId == principal.id.

title: SpEL Expressions in Security
question: What Spring Expression Language (SpEL) expressions are available in @PreAuthorize? Give examples of common expressions.
realWorldScenario: Complex access rules like 'admin OR owner of resource' need SpEL in @PreAuthorize.
